name: The Weeknd
label: XO/Republic
lede: He posted three songs under a username with no face, folded shirts at American Apparel, and ended up with the song that sat in the Hot 100 top ten for a year.

eras.title: Kin Kane in Parkdale
eras.text: Abel Tesfaye drops out at 17, moves into a Parkdale apartment with friends and folds shirts at American Apparel. He posts songs with no name, no face and no interviews, and by the end of 2010 Toronto is asking who it is.

years.h: Anonymous songs go up on YouTube
years.p: Abel Tesfaye was 19 and had already dropped out of school, sold cannabis and worked the floor at an American Apparel. He moved to Parkdale on a weekend and cut the last 'e' off the word to dodge a trademark.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Tesfaye left school at 17, lived on welfare checks in Parkdale with his friend [[La Mar Taylor|280b5ad7-c54d-4527-b746-d91a4672d157]] (now his creative director), and went through homelessness and jail before the music took off. Earlier aliases included Kin Kane, from the hip-hop duo Bulleez n Nerdz, and he had been part of a production team called the Noise.

The name comes from the move: he went to Parkdale on a weekend and dropped the final 'e' from 'weekend' to avoid clashing with a Canadian pop rock band called the Weekend.

years.cap: The Weeknd en el festival Lollapalooza Chile, celebrado el 1 y 2 de abril en el parque… · Wikimedia
years.h: Three songs, one username, and Drake notices
years.p: Uploaded as xoxxxoooxo: 'What You Need', 'Loft Music' and 'The Morning'. [[Drake|9fff2f8a-21e6-47de-a2b8-7f449929d43f]] wrote about them on his blog, and the first famous fan was in.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports the three uploads picked up press from Pitchfork and the New York Times without a face or a name attached. The Weeknd did not do interviews yet.

Producer [[Jeremy Rose|33874ca1-1dba-427c-9c0f-93b38117e3a7]], who met Tesfaye at a party in 2010, co-produced songs from this period; [[Illangelo|faf9c4c1-fa6c-45a7-bd51-e91d8eed5577]] and [[Doc McKinney|f15651b5-67ab-43f5-8bb6-5a1138759e9e]] became his main producers in early 2011.

eras.title: Three mixtapes, no face
eras.text: In one calendar year Tesfaye releases three free mixtapes that rebuild R&B out of dream pop, post-punk and trip hop. He turns up as a voice on Drake's record before most people have seen him.

years.h: Drake posts 'Wicked Games' two weeks before the mixtape
years.p: Drake put the song on his site on March 7 and the anonymous singer became a mystery with an audience. Some fans thought the Weeknd was a group.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports that the secrecy fed the curiosity: for a while it was not clear whether the Weeknd was one person or a collective.

The song is on House of Balloons, which came out two weeks later.

years.src: Wikipedia: House of Balloons · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: House of Balloons, free and self-released
years.p: Illangelo and Doc McKinney produced most of it, with Jeremy Rose and Cirkut on other tracks. It made the 2011 Polaris Prize shortlist.
years.xp:
Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and called the production 'incredibly lush, downcast'. Metacritic averaged 87 across 16 reviews.

Exclaim! credited it with helping transform R&B, and the Fader's 2016 retrospective said it gave pop a new framework.

years.h: OVO Fest, a Mod Club show, and an HBO trailer
years.p: Drake was in the crowd at the Mod Club in Toronto, and the Weeknd played Drake's OVO Fest on July 31. 'High For This' turned up in an HBO Entourage promo the same month.

years.h: Thursday and Echoes of Silence finish the trilogy
years.p: Thursday came out August 18 and Echoes of Silence on December 21, both free. Echoes was long-listed for the 2012 Polaris Prize.

eras.title: The major-label handshake
eras.text: Republic Records signs him in September 2012 and XO becomes a subsidiary. The mixtapes get cleaned up and sold as Trilogy, then the first real studio album lands a little colder.

years.h: Signs with Republic Records
years.p: XO, the label he co-founded with Sal Slaiby and Cash Esmailian, becomes a Republic subsidiary. He starts his first tour, including opening dates for Florence and the Machine.

years.src: Wikipedia: Trilogy (The Weeknd album) · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: Trilogy puts the three mixtapes on sale
years.p: The three mixtapes were remastered, with three new songs: 'Twenty Eight', 'Valerie' and 'Till Dawn (Here Comes the Sun)'. It debuted at No. 4 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Selling the mixtapes meant clearing samples, including Beach House and Siouxsie and the Banshees, according to Wikipedia. An Aaliyah sample was left out of the commercial release.

Pitchfork gave it 8.5 and called it 'some of the best music of the young decade'. Wikipedia says some critics found the runtime indulgent.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kiss Land · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: Kiss Land, the tour-life horror movie
years.p: Tesfaye cited John Carpenter, David Cronenberg and Ridley Scott. It debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200, and Pitchfork gave it 6.2.
years.xp:
Metacritic's score is 65 from 31 reviews. Wikipedia says reviewers liked the atmosphere and his falsetto, but some heard a re-run of the mixtape sound.

He toured it in theaters that fall, then opened for Drake in Europe and Justin Timberlake in North America.

eras.title: Fifty Shades, then the radio
eras.text: A movie single, an Oscar nomination and three No. 1-level songs in one summer. The dark-room mixtape singer becomes a pop star without changing his voice.

years.h: 'Earned It' and an Oscar nomination
years.p: The Fifty Shades of Grey song peaked at No. 3 on the Hot 100 and earned him his only Academy Award nomination, for Best Original Song. It won him a Grammy for Best R&B Performance.

years.h: 'The Hills' and 'Can't Feel My Face' go No. 1
years.p: 'The Hills' (May 27) and 'Can't Feel My Face' (June 8) both reached No. 1 on the Hot 100. He also held all three top spots on the Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart at once, a first.
years.xp:
'The Hills' was later certified diamond by the RIAA, his first diamond-certified song, according to Wikipedia. Apple Music introduced him alongside Drake as a face of the service.

Both songs are on Beauty Behind the Madness, which followed on August 28.

years.h: Beauty Behind the Madness debuts at No. 1
years.p: 412,000 units in its first week, and it was the most-streamed album of 2015 with over 60 million streams. It won Best Urban Contemporary Album at the Grammys.
years.xp:
Wikipedia reports it reached No. 1 in Canada, Australia, Norway and the UK and was nominated for Album of the Year.

Kanye West produced 'Tell Your Friends' on it, and he headlined Lollapalooza and Bumbershoot for it.

eras.title: Starboy, melancholy, and the lights
eras.text: Daft Punk, a Kendrick Lamar duet, a trilogy-era comeback EP and a song that refuses to leave the charts. The haircut changes first and the sound follows.

years.h: 'Starboy' with Daft Punk goes No. 1
years.p: Wikipedia lists it as his third No. 1. Daft Punk are credited on the single.

years.h: Starboy is his second straight No. 1 album
years.p: 348,000 units in its first week, and another Grammy for Best Urban Contemporary Album. A short film, M A N I A, came with it.
years.xp:
He took it on the Legend of the Fall Tour through 2017, per Wikipedia.

'I Feel It Coming' peaked at No. 4 on the Hot 100.

years.h: 'Pray for Me' with Kendrick Lamar
years.p: The Black Panther song peaked at No. 7 on the Hot 100.

years.h: My Dear Melancholy, six songs, No. 1
years.p: 169,000 units made it the shortest album by track count to top the Billboard 200 in eight years. 'Call Out My Name' reached No. 4.
years.xp: He headlined Coachella for the first time on April 13, two weeks after the EP came out.

years.h: 'Blinding Lights' lands, and never really leaves
years.p: It peaked at No. 1 and became the first song to hold a top-ten spot for a full year on the Hot 100. By November 2021 Billboard ranked it the best-performing song in the chart's history.
years.xp:
'Heartless' came out two days earlier and also reached No. 1. 'Blinding Lights' spent 90 weeks on the Hot 100, the longest run by a solo artist, and was the most-streamed song on Spotify by January 2023, says Wikipedia.

A Mercedes-Benz commercial teased it on November 24, 2019.

eras.title: The red suit
eras.text: After Hours gives him a character: a red blazer, a bloody nose and a Las Vegas hangover. The Grammys ignore it, he says so in public, and then he plays the Super Bowl with his own money.

years.src: Wikipedia: After Hours (The Weeknd album) · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: After Hours and the man with the bloody face
years.p: He led the Billboard 200 and Hot 100 at once in its first week. It became the most-streamed R&B album of all time, passing his own Starboy.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the red-suited character was inspired by Fear and Loathing in Las Vegas and Joker. Producers included [[Max Martin|6622a50e-5206-44d0-9ad5-96047a726dcf]], [[Metro Boomin|59db3d82-86ea-451f-881f-dffc8ec387c9]], [[Illangelo|faf9c4c1-fa6c-45a7-bd51-e91d8eed5577]] and [[Oneohtrix Point Never|9cea062d-d476-447f-98b4-e67e14bfd1e4]].

He said the title refers to thoughts and emotions late at night, between 3 a.m. and 5 a.m.

years.big: 'Corrupt', he called the Grammys, and pulled his performance.
q: I have three GRAMMYs, which mean nothing to me now.
years.h: Zero Grammy nominations for After Hours
years.p: The 63rd Grammys nominated neither the album nor 'Blinding Lights'.
years.xp:
He later told Billboard: 'I have three GRAMMYs, which mean nothing to me now.' The Recording Academy subsequently eliminated its private nominating committees, according to Wikipedia.

He also said his label would stop submitting his work.

years.h: Super Bowl LV: first Canadian solo headliner
years.p: Wikipedia reports he put about $7 million of his own money into the show. It drew three Emmy nominations.
years.xp:
The Highlights, his second greatest hits album, came out two days earlier and debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200.

Streams of After Hours and seven other performed songs jumped after the show.
years.cap: A portrait of The Weeknd by photographer Brian Ziff · Wikimedia

years.src: Wikipedia: House of Balloons · Wikipedia: The Weeknd
years.h: The 2011 mixtapes come back with their original samples
years.p: For the tenth anniversary he re-released House of Balloons (March), Thursday (August) and Echoes of Silence (December) in their original form.

years.h: 'Take My Breath' opens the next chapter
years.p: It was released with NBC Sports around the Tokyo Olympics and peaked at No. 6 on the Hot 100.

eras.title: Purgatory radio
eras.text: He said the After Hours are done and the dawn is coming. Dawn FM turns the album into a fake radio station for the dead, with Jim Carrey as host.

years.src: Metacritic: Dawn FM · Wikipedia: Dawn FM
years.h: Dawn FM: Pitchfork's No. 11 album of 2022
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.0, calling it the Weeknd's most ambitious project in sound and scope. It debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 in the UK, Canada and Australia.
years.xp:
He described it as a purgatory radio station: 'Picture the album being like the listener is dead.' It was recorded in Los Angeles and Stockholm in 2020 and 2021.

Metacritic scored it 88 from 24 reviews, per Wikipedia. The Guardian, Rolling Stone and NME gave it five stars; the Guardian ranked it No. 3 of 2022, Billboard No. 8 and Pitchfork No. 11.

Jim Carrey is the radio host, with voice parts from Quincy Jones and Josh Safdie. Producers include Oneohtrix Point Never, Max Martin, Calvin Harris and Swedish House Mafia; Tyler, the Creator and Lil Wayne guest.

years.h: Second Coachella headline, with Swedish House Mafia
years.p: He performed with the trio who sat on Dawn FM and on 'Moth to a Flame'.

years.h: The After Hours til Dawn stadium tour starts
years.p: Wikipedia says it became the highest-grossing tour by a male soloist.

eras.title: Hurry up, tomorrow
eras.text: A TV series, a film, a stated wish to retire the name and a sixth album that opens at No. 1. The Weeknd keeps the name.

years.h: He says he might retire the Weeknd name
years.p: He said the next album could be a final hurrah under the name, and that he might go by his birth name or a new pseudonym.

years.h: The Idol arrives on HBO and gets poor reviews
years.p: He co-created it with Sam Levinson and starred with Lily-Rose Depp; HBO cancelled it on August 28 after one season. Wikipedia reports the reviews were widely negative.

years.h: Hurry Up Tomorrow is his fifth No. 1 album
years.p: 490,500 units in its first week, his biggest opening by overall units. It includes 'Timeless' with Playboi Carti.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says 359,000 of those were pure sales, the most for a male artist since 2020.

'São Paulo' with Anitta followed in October 2024.

years.h: The companion film bombs
years.p: Directed by Trey Edward Shults, with Jenna Ortega, it made about $7.6 million on a $15 million budget, according to Wikipedia. Critics mostly panned it.

years.h: Six straight nights at the Stade de France
years.p: Wikipedia reports six consecutive sold-out shows in Paris in July 2026.
